review_notes: I read the whole target file and the definitions it relies on: AngleIndependentJet, history, velocityJet, knownJets, slowAdvection, fastAdvection and nonlinearGrade. I also grepped for other uses. The file has no @[simp] attributes of its own. The weakness is in the interface of the upstream definitions: there are no case or apply equation lemmas, so each proof re-unfolds the definitions with `simp only [knownJets, history, ...]` or `change`. I did not run Lean. Whether the proposed lemmas would be good simp lemmas depends on the hypothesis forms. I suggest `hi : i < p` as a side condition that simp can discharge, or `@[simp]` only on the unconditional equations. I did not claim any loop or simp failure.

findings.problem: `knownJets`, `history` and `velocityJet` have no equation or case lemmas stating `knownJets O p a z i = velocityJet … i` for `i < p`, `= slicedJet … (a (p-1)).corrector z` for `i = p`, and `= 0` for `i > p`. Each of the three branches here therefore unfolds the definitions by hand with a different `simp only` list of `knownJets, history, velocityJet, ite_true, ite_false` and so on. The same unfolding lists are copied in PacketCylinderKnownJets.lean, PacketCylinderForcingParity.lean, PacketResidualTailFields.lean, PacketRecursiveCancellation.lean and PacketProfileTailGrade.lean. This unfolding also exposes the `if i=0 then 0 else …` structure of `velocityJet` to the simplifier. The lists depend on the internal `if` layout, and `hz`, `hi` and `he` must be supplied by hand.
findings.proposed_change: In PacketProfileRecursion.lean, next to `history` and `knownJets`, add equation lemmas for the three cases. For example, `history_of_lt (h : i < p) : history p u c i = u i`, `history_self : history p u c p = c`, and `history_of_gt (h : p < i) : history p u c i = 0`. Add matching `knownJets` lemmas and `velocityJet_zero` and `velocityJet_of_ne_zero (h : i ≠ 0)`. Mark the hypothesis-conditioned ones @[simp] where side conditions are dischargeable by `simp`/`omega`, and state the `i = 0` and `i = p` cases without a side condition. The branches here can then be written as `rw [knownJets_of_lt hi, velocityJet_of_ne_zero hz]` or a plain `simp [hi, hz]`, with no `ite_true`/`ite_false` bookkeeping.
findings.benefit: There would be one canonical normal form for known jets. The several proofs that currently hand-unfold the `if` chains would shrink and would no longer break when `history` or `velocityJet` is restructured. The simp sets in downstream files would also become uniform.

findings.problem: `EulerPacketPointJets.slowAdvection` and `fastAdvection` are bundled `LinearMap`s built with anonymous constructors. They have no `_apply` simp lemmas, so their values cannot be rewritten by `simp` or `rw`. The proofs here work around this with `change` to a hand-written `K.2 (spatialInjection (A θ (J θ).1))` or `inner ℝ m J.1 • (K θ).2 angleDirection`. Elsewhere the same gap is handled with `simp only [fastAdvection, LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk, hK, smul_zero]`, for example in `fastAdvection_angleConstant_right`. Here `fastAdvection_zero` repeats the content of `fastAdvection_angleConstant_right` (a vanishing angular derivative on the right gives 0), but it is proved by a separate `change` and not by that lemma.
findings.proposed_change: Next to the definitions in PacketPointJets.lean, add @[simp] lemmas `slowAdvection_apply (FInv J K) : slowAdvection FInv J K = K.2 (spatialInjection (FInv J.1))` and `fastAdvection_apply (m J K) : fastAdvection m J K = ⟪m, J.1⟫_ℝ • K.2 angleDirection`. Both are provable by `rfl`. Then `slowAdvection` here becomes `simp only [slowAdvection_apply, hA θ, hJ.value θ, hK.spatial θ]`. `fastAdvection_zero` becomes `fastAdvection_angleConstant_right m J _ (hK.angular θ)`. The `change` steps can be deleted.
findings.benefit: The bundled-linear-map definitions get a stable applied form. The proofs stop depending on defeq-through-`change`, and the `LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk` clutter disappears from every call site. The duplicated lemma `fastAdvection_zero` collapses to the existing one.
